newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former S.Korean security chief faces arrest - TV.
newsitem.headline: Former S.Korean security chief faces arrest - TV.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Sunday sought the arrest of a former top security official close to the son of President Kim Young-sam, Yonhap Television News reported.
It said Kim Ki-sup would be charged with accepting bribes and influence-peddling. A prosecution official said he could not immediately confirm the report.
The president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, was arrested on Saturday and detained on charges of taking kickbacks and evading taxes.

Yonhap said prosecutors asked a Seoul court to issue an arrest warrant for Kim Ki-sup on charges of taking 150 million won ($168,000) from a former top executive of Daeho Construction Co in return for help obtaining a cable television licence.
The president's son was earlier charged with accepting 1.7 billion won from the same businessman, and taking 1.5 billion won from another business associate.

Kim Ki-sup was a senior manager at a five-star Seoul hotel before being given the number two job at the Agency for National Security Planning after President Kim took power. He had been a loyal supporter of Kim Young-sam.
